top_story.headline: Quiet Sunday in contracting: the Air Force asks for weaponized small drones and plans a navigation-warfare lab
top_story.dek: No sole-source justifications, nothing tied to the White House or Washington, D.C., and no new apportionments.
paragraphs: The most notable item in today's contracting data is an Air Force Life Cycle Management Center request for information on domestically produced small uncrewed aircraft carrying kinetic (weaponized) payloads. According to the statement of objectives, the Air Force wants production-ready systems in three weight classes: Group 1 (up to 20 pounds), Group 2 (20 to 55 pounds) and Group 3 (55 to 1,320 pounds). The file was posted October 20 and was read today.

Separately, the Air Force Test Center at Arnold Air Force Base asked industry for whitepapers on an Advanced Navigation Simulation Environment Laboratory, an effort to modernize simulation of position, navigation and timing and navigation warfare, using other transaction authority rather than a standard contract.

sections.headline: Air Force seeks industry whitepapers for a navigation-warfare simulation laboratory at Arnold Air Force Base
paragraphs: Two new solicitations were posted; two repeats from earlier editions were left out. Both new ones are written up below.

blocks.title: Air Force Test Center asks industry for whitepapers on a navigation-warfare simulation laboratory
blocks.text: The Air Force Test Center at Arnold Air Force Base seeks engineering, technical and integration support to modernize its position, navigation and timing and navigation warfare simulation capability. The request goes to members of the AEDC Velocity Alliance Consortium and other industry partners and uses 10 U.S.C. § 4022 other transaction authority, which sits outside standard contracting rules. No value is given, and the one attached file has not been read yet.

blocks.title: FEMA seeks armed guards for its Florida long-term recovery offices
blocks.text: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Region 4 is soliciting Level II armed guard security services, on a labor-hour basis, for its Long Term Recovery Office sites in Lake Mary and Fort Myers, Florida, supporting disaster DR4834. Questions are due October 29. The notice is an amendment adding omitted evaluation-factor documents. Its 11 attached files are queued for reading.

sections.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement exercises a $29.4 million option on its medical claims processing contract
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

13 new awards of $2 million or more (none from the Defense Department's 90-day backlog), 1 large modification and 1 cut. Two of the awards, tied to Washington, D.C., are in that section. The 11 routine ones are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Acentra Health LLC received a $29,393,066 modification from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement on October 23. It exercises option period 1 (modification P00006) on a contract to provide the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Health Service Corps with medical claims processing support. (award)

Jimenez Engineering Solutions, LLC won $3,185,000 from the General Services Administration's Public Buildings Service for design and construction at the Border Patrol Big Bend District Station on West Madrid Street in Marfa, Texas. The project covers two new modular buildings and the demolition of another. (award)

Vantor Services Inc. received $4,398,855 from the Department of the Interior's Departmental Offices to expand the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for forensic analysis of historic and new data, aimed at identifying "extremely low frequency suspect activities not currently known to be occurring." The description does not say what activity is meant. (award)

items: Labels & Lists Inc — $950,000, Department of Commerce (U.S. Census Bureau): commercial voter registration data; the description gives no further detail on its use (award).
TIMS 8A JV LLC — $354,151, Department of Homeland Security (U.S. Customs and Border Protection): tactical infrastructure maintenance in the El Paso and Big Bend North areas (award).

CoreCivic, Inc. — $929,066, Department of Justice (Bureau of Prisons): residential reentry center services in Newport News, Virginia, and home confinement services in the Eastern District of Virginia, an option year (award).
Mustansir Barma — $332,510, United States Trade and Development Agency: a personal services contract for a regional manager for Africa, based in Johannesburg, South Africa (award).
TM3 Solutions, Inc. — $166,130, Department of Homeland Security (Federal Emergency Management Agency): aerial imagery and geospatial labor for the Guam tropical cyclone disaster response (award).
Artemis Creek, LLC — $143,277, Department of State: information technology support for a G20 conference (award).
